posts.description: Each book that a user has read can have a number next to it that is the average number of pages they read per day when reading it. It can toggle between: * total pages divided by number of days between start and end date. * total pages divided by the number of days the user read that book.

posts.title: Allow correcting covers as part of wrong information form
posts.description: The "report missing information" form does not allow to upload any images if a cover already exists, so there's no easy way to transfer the correct cover to the volunteer librarians. As a workaround, sending a link seems to work, but it requires uploading the image somewhere first if it can't already be found online. (This may be a bigger issue for non-English books, since alternative language editions seem to often end up with very random assignments, sometimes not even corresponding to the right book.)

posts.title: track short stories without inflating stats
posts.description: I want to add short stories and have the pages count, but I don't want each to count as a "book" and inflate my books read per year, etc.

posts.title: Stats on series pages
posts.description: I would love more information or statistics on the series pages. Like, for example, the status of the series (ongoing, unfinished, finished etc.), year of first and latest part, authors and contributors (like illustrators for a comic), how many parts there are, original language, number of languages it's available in on TSG, which part has the highest/lowest score, average score for the whole series, how many users have read the series and so on. Would be really fun!

posts.title: More features in custom charts
posts.description: I’d like the ability to use themes/moods/genres/book format that are already stored on the books in custom charts instead of having to use only custom tags. I.e. I’d like to compare the Young Adult Genre with my ‘Not YA’ custom tag And a pie chart of paperback vs hardback books etc

posts.title: stats by author
posts.description: I would love an option to see stats by an author, similar to being able to see stats specific to tag.

posts.title: Make it easer to get to the roadmap from the app
posts.description: I'd like for there to be an easier way for plus members to get to the roadmap from the main storygraph page or account settings.

posts.title: “Contained Books” (for collections and split editions)
posts.description: Hi! 👋 I’d love a feature that lets us link books that are part of a larger collection or split into multiple volumes. Right now, StoryGraph shows “You’ve read another edition” if you read a different version of the same book - which is great! But this doesn’t work well when: • A single book is split into several parts across different editions. → Example: The Count of Monte Cristo is sometimes published in 3 separate volumes. • Or when multiple short works are grouped into one collection. → Example: Lady Susan, The Watsons, Sanditon is often published together, but also exists as three separate books. It would be amazing to have a “contained books” option, where you can: • Link smaller books that make up a bigger one (or vice versa). • Automatically mark a collection as “read” once all its parts are read. • Automatically mark contained works as “read” if you finish the full collection. • See something like “You’ve read this as part of a collection” when viewing a linked title. This would make reading stats, challenges, and collections much more accurate - especially for classics, anthologies, and multi-volume works. Thank you so much for considering it! 💛

posts.title: Librarian Mode Toggle
posts.description: I'd like to have a toggle so that I can either be browsing books as a fellow reader or as a StoryGraph librarian. This would toggle on/off some features in the drop-downs such as 'make this a main book' so that it's not so easy to mis-click when I'm trying to switch which edition I'm reading! Having them in the same menu when I'm not navigating the app in "librarian mode" mentally stresses me out and I'd like a little "safety mode" where it's just the simplified user options.

posts.title: Sort currently reading by progress
posts.description: I’d love to be able to sort my currently reading by progress so I can prioritize books easier

posts.title: Add question for "Weight" in rating
posts.description: Would love to have an option for light/medium/heavy overall weight of a book. Keep it loose, this could be density of prose, political intrigue, depth of world, or just general vibes.

posts.title: Add DNFs to Monthly Wrap Graphics
posts.description: Add DNFs to Monthly Wrap Graphics for covers/ratings.

posts.title: TBR Info in Wrap-Up
posts.description: At would be really nice to have a stat in the end of year (or monthly) wrap-up that says "you read X amount of books off of your TBR this year" and have it also give the average amount of time those books spent on your TBR.

posts.title: Challenges with start date but no end date
posts.description: Would like the ability to make challenges have a start date so it doesn’t count books before a certain period but also isn’t tied to an end date

posts.title: Filter my TBR to books on my friends TBR
posts.description: I am always looking for books that my friends have on their TBR too so we can read them together without having to try and manually find books we both want to read (since my TBR has over 800 books currently). And I think this may be on other suggestions so just adding it to the bottom here. Being able to filter the TBR for standalones. Thank you!

posts.title: Monthly wrap-up calendar on stats page
posts.description: I LOVE LOVE LOVE the new monthly wrap-up calendar. Before I’d check my streaks and the month-by-month stats graphic, but this calendar is perfect to visualize my daily reading. I find myself generating calendars often. I would adore if the current month had a static, automatically updating place on the main stats page. Right now it requires several clicks and loading which is fine, but it’s so amazing I’d love to have it be more accessible!

posts.title: Make app tabs more easily navigable
posts.description: Currently when you're switchgng between tabs in the app, the page you were previously on reloads so you can't go back to it; for example if I'm scrolling through my TBR from the homepage, or was on a book page from the recommendations list, if I switched over to the stats tab, there's no way to go back to where I was; clicking the Home tab just brings me back to the home page again instead of the page I was previously on in that tab. It's a bit counterintuitive, and makes it harder to do more than one thing at a time in the app

posts.title: Add books from tag page
posts.description: Currently, in a reading challenge, you are able to add books to a prompt in a search bar within the prompt page (see first pic). It would be great if we could do that for tags as well to make at-scale tagging easier; right now there's only searching within the tag (see second pic).

posts.title: Set language preferences for books
posts.description: Users would have the ability to set the default book language in their preferences. For example, if a user says 30 default language to English in preferences, only English editions would show up in the edition section of a book.

posts.title: Add Read vs TBR Plot in Owned books
posts.description: I'm not sure how common this is, but I have owned books in my home library which I want to inventory in TheStoryGraph, but don't necessarily want to read them. That means that currently my read/unread plot is a bit useless because a lot of the "unread" aren't on my TBR. So it doesn't really give me the purpose this plot was made for (I think), which I interpreted as "how many books have I read out of all the books I own and want to read" Basically I think the assumption of this plot is that all books owned must necessarily be in the TBR pile and this isn't necessarily true for all people. So a possible suggestion would be to make that distinction with an additional plot: Owned books: Read vs Unread Owned books: Read vs TBR Obviously for some people, they would be exactly the same, but for others the later plot would give them much more information to understand how close they are to having a 0% owned TBR. Thank you in advance for your consideration!

posts.title: Streak pause ability
posts.description: I would love a feature to be able to pause my streak progress (similar to what Duolingo has) for when I am on vacation or other kinds of planned divergences from my usual reading routine.

posts.title: Emoji reactions to reviews
posts.description: Would be cool if people could allow emoji reactions on their reviews, similar to buddy read reactions—maybe with a setting like “who can react to my reviews?” and options “friends, followers, no one, etc”

posts.title: More page option splits in the charts
posts.description: On the how many pages pie chart, I've just read a 960 page book however that's included in the 500+ category. It would be great to see them broken down slightly smaller as there's a huge difference between a 500 page book and a 900 page book so would be good to see that illustrated better

posts.title: Character tracker
posts.description: Some books have so many characters, and I haven't found a great way to keep track of them all. I'd love a character tracker feature for Storygraph, with options for description of the character and plot points involving the character!

posts.title: Add all titles by author or series
posts.description: It would be nice to be able to add all the books that are not already on my TBR by an author or that are in a series instead of adding one by one. So for example, if I just read a book by Stephen King and loved it, I could then go and add his entire catalog to my TBR.

posts.title: More author info when adding a new book
posts.description: When adding a book, if there is more than one author with the same name it's really tricky to identify which one is which. In some cases I know these may be accidental duplicates of the same author, but in others it's just the same name. It would be good if, when selecting the author, some useful information such as their most popular other books were shown so we can easily identify which is the correct one.

posts.title: Sort reading challenges
posts.description: Hi there, it would be helpful on the main reading challenge page to be able to sort by incomplete/no book added, similar to how it is when you go to “add book to reading challenge” on the book page. This would make it easier to see which prompts are incomplete.

posts.title: Stats filtered down by language
posts.description: In the Viewing Stats For dropdown, I would love the option to specify which of my language(s) the stats are for.

posts.title: Percent Read vs. Unread pages for all Currently Reading books
posts.description: This might only be useful to people who read a lot of books at once, but I think it would be neat if somewhere there was a stat that showed up on your currently reading page that had the total number of pages for all of the books you're currently reading, and then how many you'd read and how many pages you had to go. I'm kind of thinking of an overall percent read for all the books you're currently reading. I can see this getting applied to tags, too, with a percent read number for each tag. Nothing urgent or life-shattering, I just think it would be neat.

posts.title: Personal Ratings
posts.description: My partner and I don't like to publicly rate books, but think it would helpful to have some kind of personal rating system where we, for example, mark books as "liked," "ambivalent," or "disliked." This way when we go back and look at our read books it's easier for us to remember (and then recommend) what we enjoyed without having to publicly rate the books.

posts.title: “Listen to X minutes” or “Read X pages” reading challenges
posts.description: This was inspired by the January pages challenge—it would be really great to be able to set a shared minutes or pages goal with a friend via a reading challenge, with a time limit shorter than a year (a month, say), and see how we’re both progressing towards it. These could be a different category of reading challenge!

posts.title: A way to "finish" Challenges after their end date
posts.description: I regrettably did not complete most of the challenges I had set up for last year. I don't necessarily want to archive the challenges right now, because I do not want the books I had picked to vanish into the ether of my (very long) TBR. I would love an option on Challenges that have an end date that basically says "would you like to keep working on this challenge?" and allows me to see my progress in a way that is differentiated from the reading that happened during the initial time-frame of the challenge. I threw together a mock-up, the language on the second line is definitely confusing and not what I think the copy should actually be haha, but just to give an idea.

posts.title: Update Book Progress on Buddy Read Page
posts.description: Would like to be able to update current place in the book from the buddy reads page. Typically, the buddy read page will be open as I'm adding comments. Would be nice in the top section showing where each person is at percentage wise to be able to hit edit right there.

posts.title: Reading Challenges on Book Page
posts.description: I think it would be nice to see on a book's page if anyone has read that book for an open reading challenge. Right now, I look at the reading challenges and, even categorized, it's overwhelming, but if I'm reading a book and I can easily see some of the challenges it's on, that'd be a handy way to highlight a subset of challenges for me to consider.

posts.title: Explain why a book was recommended
posts.description: I'd love to see why a book was recommended to me. Was it similar to other books I've read (which ones!)? Popular in genres I like? Loved by users similar to me?

posts.title: Separating format/medium from genre
posts.description: I would love it if there was a dedicated stat for prose/audiobook/manga/graphic novels, because that is just as useful as whether something is digital or hardcopy. At the very least: manga, graphic novels, and comics are not a genre. They're a medium or a format, as you prefer. Please can we take them out of the genre section?

posts.title: Reading Goals on Community Tab
posts.description: I'd love it if the community tab had a post when someone I follow hits their page/book goal for the year! I want to be able to see that and celebrate it within the app.

posts.title: more community engagement
posts.description: engaging more with the community without having to search or browse for friends or be in a buddy read. it’s a little lonely on this app right now and i would like to have discussions with people about books or as questions or thoughts and theories

posts.title: Option to Share Reading Journal Entries
posts.description: I would really like the option to share parts of my reading journal. I was thinking this would be good if the reading journal updates had a checkbox to add it to the review and then on the review page for that book if the reading journal entries could show up either in a slightly lighter text or to be a bit smaller than the review. Something to separate it from the review but to still allow me to share my reading progress/updates. This would be great for me because I don't really do buddy reads but I enjoy going back and looking at friends' updates and thoughts throughout the book and this would be an easy way to share that.

posts.title: Graph for reading history/pages read over time for specific books
posts.description: A graph for each book that shows updates, pages read, etc over the time that I have been reading the book. For exaple, I'd been reading The Brothers Karamazov since 2020 (and still not finished) but would like a graph that shows my progress with the book over time and when i read the most pages, etc.

posts.title: Sort Browse results by # of reviews, avg review, etc.
posts.description: When browsing, even with a filtered browse, it would be very useful to be able to **sort** by popularity. "Popular this week" is more of a filter, and for me it typically yields "We don't have anything that matches that criteria."

posts.title: List books in a series in order
posts.description: It would be great when clicking on or searching a series if the books could appear in chronological/series order.

posts.title: Split Fantasy Genre
posts.description: Split Fantasy Genre into "Fantasy", "Paranormal" and "Urban Fantasy". I think it would greatly help with recommendations and with ISBN auto populations I've noticed most paranormal books do not auto populate the fantasy genre when that is the closest it fits to available

posts.title: Averaging pages read
posts.description: HHiHi! For the pages read stat, for those users that don't track daily pages read, the graph goes from several days of zero pages, to "dumping" all the pages of the book on the day you've marked it finished. OI think the graph would look much nicer if the app would instead lfoflfof putting all the book's pages on the day it's finished, average them out from the day the user started reading.

posts.title: Social Media Post Templates
posts.description: What I'd love to see is the ability to share certain information to social media once you've finished a book, preferably in image form. To accompany reviews you may post out.

posts.title: Exclude certain authors from recommendations
posts.description: ooption to list authors you do not want to appear in your recommendation list

posts.title: Author names in different languages
posts.description: Since author names appear differently in different languages, it would probably be good to consolidate different versions under one - so it would appear during search regardless of its spelling (e.g. whether it's Jo Walton (English), Джо Уолтон (Russian) or whatever it looks like in, for example, Chinese). Right now if I search for Джо Уолтон, I won't get any hits, but if I search for her book "Среди других" (Among Others) - I will. So, aside from gathering various spelling/languages under one heading, it might be also prudent to display the author's name in the language the book is under.

posts.title: Page Count for Non-books / Private "books"
posts.description: I read a lot of scientific papers and articles, and I wish I could include these in the pages count. I think that managing entries for non-standardazied formats would be way too much for the Librarians (until your API is ready to dance with CrossRef's?), but I think a possible solution would be to have a blank/custom book option that would not be publicly searchable that could count toward one's stats and goals. The book length could be measured in time (for audiobooks & podcasts), pages, or words (with either a standardized or customizable conversion to a pagenum). I think this may be valuable for people who read daily periodical digests, and even more so for fan-fiction readers.

posts.title: Add ability to search and filter reading journal
posts.description: It would be awesome if the reading journal were searchable/filterable.

posts.title: Following "Plus" (friends, narrower sort)
posts.description: Can we have the ability to designate some of the "People you follow" as "starred"/special ... perhaps for friends I know in real life, or those whose activities I especially want to follow closely? Thx!

posts.title: Option to filter by books not yet read
posts.description: Right now, when I search a tagged list, I can show books, it doesn't seem to have an option to show me books I haven't read. It would be great to filter out the books I've already read!

posts.title: Alternate Algorithms
posts.description: I've seen several posts where people are trying to read more books by more BIPOC/LGBTQIA voices, or by other languages. To aid in this, could there be a way to select alternate algorithms for the different widgets (Recommended/ TBR/ etc)? This would be an overlay on top of the regular algorithm, so the results would be skewed in a known, positive, way. I've put some options below, but you'll definitely want to talk to a larger group about this, and hopefully include some experts. Possibilities - recommend more BIPOC - Recommend more LGBTQIA - Recommend more languages (choose language) - Recommend by country/continent stats - this is one I would like, as I don't think I see a representative sample of the demographics of my country by age/race/language/etc. I also think it would be fun to pick a different country and try to read more from their stats (so not necessarily that the books would have had to have been written by someone in that country/continent - though that sounds interesting too)

posts.title: Collages and Graphics for Completing Challenges
posts.description: Just like monthly and yearly wrap-ups.

posts.title: Kobo syncing- option to open ebook without it immediately being marked as currently reading in SG
posts.description: I LOVE the kobo syncing with StoryGraph feature however sometimes I’d like to open up an ebook without it being marked as being read. Like I’m flipping through a book. For example, when I’ve just bought an ebook I might want to have a look at the contents page or after I’ve read a ebook to look back at my highlights. Maybe an option to tick a “yes I’m starting this ebook” or something?

posts.title: Kobo Highlights/Notes Saved to Journal Entries
posts.description: With the integration of Kobo x StoryGraph it would be cool to have our notes/highlights be saved in our journal entries section. I’ve started to do it manually for my Libby borrowed books and it’s a hassle.

posts.title: Cover/ratings collage also show which books are rereads
Long-term reading challenge progress shown in yearly wrap-up
posts.description: It's fun to see how many challenges I've completed, but I also participate in several long-term challenges with almost 200 prompts (e.g. Essential Women & Read around the world) and I would love to see in my yearly wrap-up how much % progress I've made on each of those!

posts.title: Search reading challenge prompts
posts.description: Especially because of challenges that have a large number of prompts, I'd like a way to search for a specific prompt in the challenge. E.g., in a "read the world" challenge, I'd have to scroll a long time to reach a particular prompt out of hundreds, and the app often freezes up with so much scrolling on one challenge. Moreover, sometimes when I select a prompt and then go back to the list of challenge prompts, I'm moved back up to the top of the list and have to scroll all the way down again. All this to say, I'd like a way to search through challenge prompts on the challenge page, like how you can search through challenge prompts when you go through the options to add a specific book to a challenge starting from the book page!

posts.title: AI summaries of reviews
posts.description: I would love to be able to see a summary of the reviews, what are common things users pick out in the book, similarly to how the ai personalised recommendations work.

posts.title: Covers on each day in calendar
posts.description: Most of the other reading apps I use have a calendar feature that has the cover(s) of each book read each day. I'd love it if the Storygraph did this too rather than color coding!

posts.title: Backup/Storygraph Import
posts.description: I do not know what to call this but I want to be able to import a Storygraph backup file the same way you can do with Goodreads backup files. I periodically save backups of all of my stuff and, if I were to ever lose access to my account, I could not imagine re-entering all of these books by hand. I am begging you to please make it an option for us to import from a Storygraph file backup.

posts.title: Bookshop.org App Integration
posts.description: Connect bookshop.org library so owned ebooks can be added to your SG library automatically and in-progress/completed reads can be added to your current and recent reads in SG automatically (or according to users' settings or preferences)

posts.title: Essay Function
posts.description: It would be nice to be able to chose specific pages of a book instead of just going chronologically for if it's a short story or essay collection, as lots of people don't always read them in order or in one go.

posts.title: 700+ Pages Statistic Addition
posts.description: It would be great to see some of our thick books get the love that they deserve in the stats section. Adding a 700+ pages statistic would be wonderful, and changing the current 500+ to “500-699 pages”

posts.title: Show rereads in community
posts.description: It's great that it now explicitly says we are re-reading something, but would love to see it say that in the community page as well!

posts.title: Keep Plant on Favorites Shelf
posts.description: I'd love the option to keep the plant on the Favorites shelf on our profile, for the trade off of showing one less favorite book. I think it's so cute!

posts.title: Read Books Owned Filter Should Ignore Edition
posts.description: When in my “recently read” or “read” section, if I select the filter “Only Show Me Books I Own” it only populates if I read the edition I own. It should show any book owned, regardless of edition read (ex. own the physical but read an audio). This would mirror how the Owned Books -> read/unread tag works, and would be easier for tracking purposes!

posts.title: Days to read based on page count chart
posts.description: Hello! I would love to see a chart related to how long (on average) it takes you to read a book based on page count. Maybe for a v1, it could be a comparison of the three lengths provided by default, but it could evolve to show more custom categories (like in Custom charts). I would like to see how long on average it takes me to read a book that's 200 pages vs 400 pages vs 600 pages.

posts.title: Add Romantasy as a genre
posts.description: I currently use a custom tag for my Romantasy reads and would love to have the option of having a specific tag instead. It would be more helpful when searching for recommendations too. 🥰

posts.title: Option to choose monthly cover collage aspect ratio
posts.description: It would be great if we could choose the aspect ratio of our cover collages to fit nicely in an Instagram post/social media post. Right now if you read over about 15 books in a month the collage image gets cropped when posting. A 3:4 (1080x1350] option would be fantastic!

posts.title: List of legend items under custom pie charts
posts.description: under the standard moods pie chart, the list of all moods is displayed, ordered by the most frequent to the last frequent, and you can select them to hide or display them. It would be nice to have the same thing under custom pie charts, possibly with a toggle to add it or not, because in pie charts with a lot of values it becomes impossible to read or select them. For example I have the attached pie chart with authors nationalities but it's not really readable without the list of values below

posts.title: Additional data in export
posts.description: There are already several tickets requesting more data to be added to the export but none I've seen that mention the ones I'm interested in. For my use I'd love to see: - Year Published (Edition) - Original Publication Year - number of pages / number of minutes (either as one field or separated) Requests that are in other tickets that I'd also love!: - An added author name column that is "Last Name, First Name" for use in filtering quickly - Genre(s) - series data

posts.title: Add Calibre Sync
posts.description: Ability to sync your calibre library with StoryGraph (and back the other way) including star ratings, notes, tags, dates read, etc.

posts.title: Comment on reading challenges
posts.description: I would love to be able to discuss books for reading challenges and/or indicate why I added a book to a reading challenge for others to view. It would also be interesting to see how many other people are using a book to complete the reading challenge.

posts.title: Table view of monthly reading for books/pages/minutes
posts.description: The line graph that displays the number of minutes/pages/books read per month is my favorite. But I wish it was easier to access totals read for months, especially for a broader timeframe. For example, if I do the custom dates of January 2024 to now, I lose that line graph. I want a quick way to be able to see books/pages/months over whatever time period I choose. While I like the line graphs in stats and with my streak, I’d love a simple table to display totals. I’m in the habit of logging my daily reading with SG now. I wish it was more accessible to see my real numbers over time without having to tap on dots on a line graph, especially as the line graphs only display certain periods of time.

posts.title: See which challenges app-wide a book has been added to (even if a user isn't part of those challenges)
posts.description: It would be awesome if the book under beta listed what challenges it has been added to in the past so we can ascertain if we want to join that challenge and also to allow us to easily add the book to a prompt. Ie. Shakespeare Macbeth might say “in reading challenge plays, reading challenge Shakespeare, reading challenge poetry”. Etc. I frequently use challenges to find other books I would want to read later. It’s similar to the shelves idea Goodreads had where you could see where other people shelved the book and browse similar moods. Filters could be challenge drop down - challenges using this book as a prompt, other books recommended from that prompt, number of challenges containing this book.

posts.title: Ability to manually edit/add a personal pages number
posts.description: Especially for ebooks, I see many different editions of a book with different page counts; but often, still none of them fit my version/edition. This leads me to two options: (a) I can add *another* version of the book, copying all the information from an already entered edition but just changing the page count, or (b) I can log the book I'm reading with a wrong page count. If it's only like 10 pages off, I usually don't care, but sometimes it's like 100 pages off. For example, I am reading Abaddon's Gate by James S. A. Corey at the moment and my ebook version is 464 pages long. There are already 5 English ebook versions of this book in the Storygraph database, but they are all 550+ pages. Logging one of these messes up my stats on a bigger scale though. It would be great to have the possibility to edit the page number (just for the personal records, doesn't have to be in the database). That way I could keep my page counts accurate :) Thank you so much for the app though. I really love it and actually open it more often than Instagram :)

posts.title: Adding to my TBR via images
posts.description: I take a lot of screenshots of instagram and pictures at book stores on my phone for me to add to my TBR later but it takes me ages to get around to it because I'll have like 50 books (some repeats) and so it would be AMAZING if I could "upload" my images into StoryGraph and then they are scanned for titles, generates a list and removes duplicates and then adds them to my TBR on here.

posts.title: Show which books I've read the most
posts.description: I'd love a way to sort my read books by the number of times I've read it or be able to see/create a stat that surfaces that information. I often re-read books when I'm sick or in need of comfort and it'd be helpful to know which books I reach for most often.

posts.title: Reading Challenge Stats
posts.description: I think it would be so cool if the creator of a public reading challenge got a statistics breakdown after the end of the challenge! With data like the number of users who finished the challenge, the book most commonly read for the challenge, etc. Just think it would be interesting and cool :D

posts.title: Monthly calendar - Less overlap of cover art if you finish more than one book on a day
posts.description: Love the monthly calendar! I would love to be able to see more of the cover art if I finish multiple books on the same day. Even if that means they need to be slightly smaller. With the way they currently overlap it can be hard to tell at a glance what book is underneath.

posts.title: Filter by Author Identities
posts.description: I’ve been trying to be more intentional in diversifying my reading. I would love if there were identity tags for authors so I could filter my TBR to only show books by women of color or LGBTQ authors, or neurodiverse authors.

posts.title: Recommendations of similar books when on a book's page
posts.description: It would be great when you're on a book's page to see other similar books/recommendations. E.g. I finish a book, write a review, and then want to find books similar to it

posts.title: Match Tag Title to Custom Chart Tag Title
posts.description: Would it be possible to link the Title for tags both in the Tag view as well as the title in Custom charts? It would simplify a lot of manual editing and ensure a cleaner look everywhere. Thanks!

posts.title: Surface all used languages in edition language filter
posts.description: Currently, the language selector when looking for an edition puts English first, and then all locales per alphabetical order. I'd like to see my selected languages in alphabetical order, and then all others, rather than just English!

posts.title: Have a way to combine Roman numeral and standard page numbers in page count
posts.description: Have a way to count Roman numerals in a book that has them along with the regular page numbers. Some books mark a prologue with Roman numerals, and then the rest of the book with regular numbers. I Attached the screenshot of a table of contents that has both Roman numerals and standard numbers for page numbers.

posts.title: Editions search
posts.description: I recently bought some classics, and wanted to log them as owned, but classics have 1000+ editions, and even searching by isbn and filtering to paperback and language, i still scrolled through 100s before giving up. I wish I could search by publisher

posts.title: Exclude To Read Books fom Recommendations
posts.description: A number of the recommendations I get are books I’ve already marked as “to read”. I’d love the option to exclude those from recommendations so I can get more recommendations for books I haven’t discovered yet. Thanks!

posts.title: Add all books from reading challenge to TBR
posts.description: It'd be great to be able to add all books from a reading challenge (e.g. a prize longlist) to my TBR in one click

posts.title: Add rereads to "Up Next"
posts.description: I wanted to remind myself that I had plans to reread a book, but I can only see the "Up Next" option on books I haven't read yet. Books I have previously marked read the option is missing. It does show up under other editions, so I will use that for now and change it when I start to read, but it isn't intuitive and if the book only has one edition it won't work.

posts.title: Shared/Collaborative Reading List
posts.description: I'd like to be able to put together a list of books that my friend (a buddy for buddy reads!) can also add books to. We have a monthly reading list and want to jointly choose books and remember the ones we both are interested in.

posts.title: Add something to recommendations to let me know why it's recommended
posts.description: I believe I would find more of a use for the recommendations given if I could see why they were being recommended. I have to assume recommendations are driven by books in my lists, but it would be very helpful if I could see which books brought the recommended books up. I have a few books in my "read" pile that I absolutely hated, for example, and how am I to know if those in some way influenced a recommendation? It's confusing. I can't take the recommendations I'm getting seriously without this.

posts.title: subtitles
posts.description: I would love for there to be a subtitle field as a lot of nonfiction titles have subtitles that get put in with the title

posts.title: Random Book selection
posts.description: I would love the ability to randomly select a book from the "to read" pile, with an optional filter for owned/not-owned, as a way to pick what to read or buy next

posts.title: See format without clicking editions
posts.description: I would love to have an icon or other simple indicator to show what format an edition is on the book page without needing to go over to the editions page.

posts.title: More Bulk Upload/Import Options
posts.description: It would be nice if we could bulk upload from other locations than GR (Library Thing, Libro.FM, Audible, Library Discovery Layers, Apple Books App, Kindle, our own tracking spreadsheets.) Even if a csv or excel template was provided to input our bulk uploaded items in then upload that to the site.

posts.title: Add Subtle White Shadow Behind Books in Dark Mode
posts.description: Similar to the subtle dark shadow in Light Mode. or even just a very thin white border, not sure what would be best. I've noticed that some of my darker-colored covers get lost and don't stand out as well.

posts.title: Filter and sort tag lists by read status and read date
posts.description: One of my most heavily used tags is for audiobooks that I either have or would like to listen to with my partner. I'd like both the ability to sort/filter by status (read vs to read) as well as a way to sort by "date read". For the former, the tag is getting bogged down by the many books we have listened to together and it's hard to find the ones that are TBR. My workaround is to make two separate tags, one for "audiobook-together-tbr" and one for "audiobook-together-read", which is a bit tedious. For the latter, he asked me last night that our current book might be his favorite in a while, and then asked what were the last five or so books we had listened to, and I didn't have an easy way of answering because the "last added to tag" sort got clogged up by some catchup I was doing in December to tag books I had forgotten about. My workaround for this is meticulously ensuring that the new "audiobook-together-read" tag is being created in chronological order, but, that isn't a terribly scalable workaround since it's subject to me remembering to manually keep it up to date.

posts.title: Sharing Stats made easier
posts.description: I love to share my graphs and milestones in social media. I'm not very fond of sharing much but each new year I share a screenshot of how I did in the previous year. I would love to see the new end of year journey we got to easily share in Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, and others.

posts.title: [STATS] No. of books started vs finished balance
posts.description: A month by month graph view of the number of books started vs finished for every month during the year (+ balance of the current number of "currently reading" books as of the last day of the month at 23:59:59). EG: [month] started, finished, "currently reading" [January] +1 book, -0 book, 1 c.r. [February] +0 book, -0 book, 1 c.r. [March] +3 books, -1 book, 3 c.r. [April] +0 book, -1 book, 2 c.r. [May] +2 books, -1 book, 3 c.r. etc. Maybe it could be visualised in a format similar to Instagram's followers number insight stats. I don't know if it's a pretty niche request (I wasn't able to find a similar request, hopefully it's not a duplicate), I love graphs and I'd love to see how every time December comes I am in the middle of 5+ books.

posts.title: Filter TBR by authors you've read before
posts.description: Sometimes I just want to read something that I'm pretty sure I'll like (cause I trust that author), but I can't find it in the mess of experiments I've added to my TBR. The up next suggestions will often include books from series or authors I've previously enjoyed, but it'd be nice to be able to see them all.

posts.title: Add Purchase Date and Location info
posts.description: New database fields accompanying the Owned flag. Purchase Date Purchase Location/Store Condition Personal/BookCrossing ID With the other site furthering its decay and removing these in the coming months it would be fantastic if we could track them here. Personally, I only use date and store, but I think the bad place is removing all four.

posts.title: Owned Filter
posts.description: I would love to have add an option to filter for "owned books". Personally, I am trying to decrease my owned TBR so it would be nice to be able to add a filter that helps me see the books that I own that may help me complete a challenge or for what I am in the mood for.

posts.title: More Accurate Diversity
posts.description: Could we make it easier to find books with diverse characters? I find that it's hard to get accurate book recommendations regarding this issue, even if i put in my preferences that i want to read about black characters (specifically female) or that I want to read books by black authors. Still in my recommendations it's hard to find the books I'm looking for. If I manage to find them, it's by luck. Even if I check personnal (or not personnalized) recommendations from books with diverse characters, most of the recs are not diverse, themselves. My suggestions would be.... 1)To be more detailed when we say that a book has a diverse cast in our reviews in the ''Diverse cast of charcters?'' slot (diverse cast how? diverse in sexuality, ethnicity, race?). And if it is diverse, what is the cast made of? Black characters? Asian characters? (even then, the terms Black and Asian include so much) Lesbian characters? Non-binary characters? Is it the main characters who are diverse? The secondary ones? Idk... I feel like diversity is such a broad term and it incompases so many things that it's hard to get accurate recommendations if there is only one box to check. And it gets a bit annoying when you realize that some books that readers deem to be diverse don't have MAIN racially diverse characters, but only secondary ones. 2) To add this feature when we go to get recommendations. Along with genre, pace, length, we should have diversity as well. This suggestion is not only for the diversity. I feel like we should have the chance to be more detailed with all recommendations. We should have the option to filter triggering topics, or to add specific things that we want to see. For example, I'm an avid romance reader, and I like to read spicy books. When I choose that I want all romance books to be rec'ed, maybe there could be an option where we can choose the level of explicity that we want. And that goes for every other genre as well (but about other things that are specific to them).

posts.title: Put link to the "end of year review page" somewhere permanent
posts.description: I love the "end of year review" page, but eventually, I will have to scroll through my notifications for quite some time to find the review page of a specific year. Manually editing the url or saving it as a bookmark in my browser is not very convenient. Which is why I would like to be able to see the links to my end of year review pages in some permanent place, I think the stats tab would be a good option for that. Display could be triggered by changing the "year" dropdown box (so the link for the currently chosen year is displayed, if it exists), or we might have a link to a list of all the "end of year review" pages we will eventually have on storygraph.

posts.title: Include Page Charts in Monthly Comparisons
posts.description: When comparing monthly stats, it would be cool to see a comparison of the pages tracked each day, similar to how yearly comparisons show a chart comparing books read each month.

posts.title: See Stats for Books that Share Multiple Tags
posts.description: Currently, we have the ability to see the stats for all of the books assigned to a single tag. I would love to be able to select multiple tags at once, and see the stats for the books that share the selected tags. For example, if I have tags for "book club" and "bipoc author", I would like to see the statistics for the books that share both of those categories.

posts.title: Not Interested
posts.description: In the category with to read, read, DNF, I would love to see not interested added. I receive recommendations from many places - this app, booktok, fb groups, Goodreads, etc. In researching a book sometimes I come across a book that I know I would never read, for example I will never read a book that has cheating. I don’t want to mark it DNF because I never actually started the book. If I can mark it as “Not Interested” if the book is recommended again I will automatically know this is something I don’t want to read.

posts.title: Delete tags from book when removing it
posts.description: If I use the button "remove book" it doesn't remove the book from my tags. I have to do that myself. It would be nice to have it deleted automatically or have a pop up screen where you can say you want to delete it from your tags as well.

posts.title: Personalized Reading Challenges
posts.description: I'd love to see a form of Reading Challenges made for a single user. I like the idea of Reading Challenges, but I struggle to find ones that encourages me to look at something new without throwing me far out of my interests. The closest I can find to this is To-Read Pile Suggestions for Plus members. In this case, the idea would be to go outside of your To-Read Pile and stick you to a schedule within a time period, like weekly or monthly. Like Recommendations and Preferences, being able to keep genres and topics excluded would help keep a challenge within a person's comfort zone. For example, I don't want a reading challenge suggesting me to read religious works. While that may be outside of my comfort zones, that wouldn't be a very enjoyable challenge. Being able to randomize based on category, maybe even to-do pile, would be helpful as well. Possible ways this could be handled: - If my statistics judge that I read a lot of fiction books, my personalized reading challenge will only give me fiction books. - If I read a lot of fiction books focused on science fiction, I might be recommended a nonfiction book detailing the evolution of science fiction media. - Categorize based on Up-Next and Recommendations? "Read this book from your recommendations this month, continue this series this month, etc." - Specify genres you'd like to focus on "Only recommend me horror and thriller books for this week/month/year." Alternatively, or as an add-on, have community Reading Challenges suggested to you based on filters that match your interests. From there on, you could edit your challenges to better fit who you are than what a robot things you are. I'd love to hear further expansion or alternate considerations on this idea! I imagine this would be far, far off into the future, but a person can only hope!

posts.title: Share Reading Challenge books
posts.description: I just filled out the Reading Randomier 2022 challenge with all of the books that I plan to use to complete the challenge next year. I was telling a friend about it and she said "send me the list!" I realized that there is no way for me to do that; if I share the link to the challenge as it appears in my URL bar, on her end it just shows up as the empty challenge. I would love a way to share the books that I've picked for the challenge prompts. It seems right now that the only way for me to accomplish this would be to take screenshots or manually copy the titles into a message.

posts.title: abridged/unabridged tag for audiobooks
posts.description: Currently there isn't any way to differentiate between "unabridged" and "abridged" audiobook editions (unless you happen to know what the different durations should be). It would be great to have an additional metadata field, especially if it was filterable.

posts.title: Confusing UI if you have read multiple versions
posts.description: I don't have many instances of this in my own library, but for books where I (for example) have listened to an audiobook and then read a print version for a re-read, the metadata gets confusing. Some examples: - The book shows up twice in my "Read" list. This is a pro and a con; it is nice to see both re-reads in that list, but it is confusing to click in to both and have them be basically separate entities. - Related to this, it doesn't seem quite right when I click in to one of those copies and have it just say "you read this once in 2021" when in actuality, I read the book itself twice. It makes me do a double take, like, wait a minute, I definitely read it twice, and then I remember that I read it twice in different editions. Again, I can see how some people would want this behavior, but I find it confusing. - The most difficult thing for me is the way that tags and reviews get associated with only one edition. With the way that I am using tags, I want it to be associated with a book, not with a particular edition of it. My use case is that I'm using a tag called "book club" to maintain a list of books that my book club read. So now, instead of just adding the generic book "Gideon The Ninth" to my book club tag, I have to decide whether I want to tag the audiobook or the print book. Related, it now looks like one version of the book doesn't have a review and one does. Again, I can see why people might want the option to rate the narration differently than a print book, but for all of my purposes, I basically want the review to be for the book, not for a particular edition.

posts.title: Hide Posts from Community Tab
posts.description: Sometimes I'll do small things like update a review for a typo, or change the star rating a little. I often don't want those to show up on my community tab, especially since it pops up as if I just reviewed the book, when really I minorly edited it. It would be great if there were a way to hide specific posts from the community tab.

posts.title: Quicker access to stats page on desktop
posts.description: The stats are one of my favorite features of StoryGraph and I wish they were easier to get to on the desktop version of the site. Ideally I could access them right from the home page, rather than having to open the site, click profile, and click stats.

posts.title: Book graphic
posts.description: I think it would be nice to have a shareable/save-able book graphic that either reflects the stats of the book or allows us to put our thoughts with the graphic. Something like what readerly or bookly does

posts.title: Reading Challenge - Prompt Request
posts.description: Can you add an overall participant completion metric under each Reading Challenge's prompt? For example if there are 10 participants, can you list the number of them who completed a book in each prompt? This gives Challenge creators insight into what is and is not being read as they create future challenges. The granularity of who is reading what isn't necessary, it would simply be nice to know what categories are well received.

posts.title: community notifications
posts.description: There are currently no external notification badges / indicator if someone you follow has liked your review, or has reviewed a book themselves - would be nice to see a feature for that.

posts.title: Filter "books similar to..."
posts.description: Would it be possible to make a filter option for the Plus option "browsing similar books"? For example so that we can manually filter out genres that are marked as a "genre I don't like" in reading preferences, or to just adjust it to our current mood

posts.title: Add books to your challenge from the book page
posts.description: As I am looking at books, I'd love to be to click "add to challenge" and then select a challenge and it adds it without me having to navigate to the challenge, and then hit edit, scroll allllll the way down to the bottom to add the book.

posts.title: Differentiate "Volumes" from "Book"
posts.description: I'll explain in a practical example: "War and Peace" is 1 book, but because it is such a large one, most publishers divide it into multiple volumes. I have the book in 4 volumes, and once read, my stats will say that I've read 4 books by Leo Tolstoy. It's not accurate, I've only read 1 book, it just so happens that it is divided in 4 physical volumes. I think we should be able to divide them in different volumes in storygraph (different ISBN, covers, page numbers, etc), but make them part of one single book, so the author stats (and other stats like moods/genres etc) are also correct.

posts.title: Custom Charts - Add multiple tags with prefix/suffix rules
posts.description: I like categorising my tags with specific prefix/suffixes: e.g., for authors I track how old they were when they published the book (auth30s, auth40s, etc.). It would be great if instead of adding the tags one by one, we can define a "rule" in custom graphs, so all current (and future!) tags with same prefix/suffix will be automatically added to the plot (e.g., auth*). With this way, when I introduce a new tag in the future, I wouldn't need to adjust my custom graph.

posts.title: Ability to search based on original language
posts.description: Id love to be able to search for book recommendations based on original language :)

posts.title: Reading Challenge combo Book Goal
posts.description: Say I want to read some spooky reads for October. I'd like to create a Challenge that has a bunch of books on it, but you complete the challenge by * reading any x books, or * reading any y pages, or * reading any z hours. In other words, it's a combo of how people set Book Goals for the year, but for a Challenge. Currently you can create a Challenge which meets the first criteria (read 5 books) but you can't create one for read 1000 pages of that set of books. Eg, I create my 2026 Spooky Reads challenge. I add 10 ghost stories and horror books to it that I'm interested in. I set the Challenge Page Goal to 1000. Once I read 1000 pages in that Challenge (whether 3 books, or 5 books, or ...), then I've completed the Challenge.

posts.title: Undo marking book as finished
posts.description: I just marked a book as finished and noticed that my streak didn't go up. I realized to my extreme dismay that I forgot to log my reading on this book yesterday. Ordinarily, I would just delete the entry I just made, log yesterday's, and re-log today's. But because I marked the book as finished, I can no longer do that. I tried to do the trick of marking the book as "reading" again, and then editing the entries that way, but I somehow ended up with no way to add the "finished" entry and have it show only one read. Or at least not that I've been able to discover. I've written in to support for this particular book and I'm hoping there's a way to set this right that isn't me screenshotting all my entries and redoing them one by one. The fact that this is such a permanent and irreversible action is honestly one of the biggest ongoing pain points for me using this app. I'm glad that there is the "are you sure?" pop up, because I used to get into situations like this more often before that got added, but there was no way for me to really tell that I shouldn't click yes until after it was done. I'm titling this "undo marking book as finished" but I'd love literally any solution that would help quickly and easily fix the data. Split existing journal entries? Add entries even in "finished"? Undo back to "Reading" within a certain time limit? Please just anything to help fix mistakes without having to incorrectly mark a book read multiple times. Because it also spams the Community Feed, it now looks like I read this three times in the span of five minutes.

posts.title: Filter Giveaways by TBR
posts.description: I'd love the ability to filter giveaways by books that are already on my TBR! If I want to read it already, I'm more likely to enter one.

posts.title: A DNF toggle for series
posts.description: I would like to request a toggle for tracking series that I've decided not to continue/finish but have finished reading books in (and maybe also to keep them out of recommendations). And possibly for standalones a way to toggle for a book I've read to not be considered for recommendations.

posts.title: Save tag on homepage
posts.description: Hi! I have a tag I reference often. Right now I have it bookmarked in my web browser because in-app requires several clicks. I’d love the ability to star or bookmark specific tags right on the homepage!

posts.title: Show Progress Percentage on profile
posts.description: I would love it if it would show the percentage bar to display our progress on each book on our profile, like it is on the homepage! It would make it real easy to peak at a friend's profile to see their progress on what they're reading also!

posts.title: Include DNFs with reviews
posts.description: I am interested in seeing whether people have DNFed a book, when I'm looking at reviews. Maybe a total number beside the number of reviews, with a link? Not including them in the list of all the reviews, but having them visible and readily available would be valuable.

posts.title: Lifetime reading goal
posts.description: It would be amazing to have a lifetime reading goal rather than, or in addition to, a yearly one. Like, a reading goal that doesn't expire.

posts.title: Custom Review Scale
posts.description: As it is now, the personalized recommendations seem to pull from your average ratings to determine what is a low or high score. However, I am more likely to choose a book I think I will like, so of course most of my books are rated 3 stars or above. This becomes a problem when the AI says something like "This book has _____ theme, which is present in your lower rated reads (Title, 3.75 stars)" If we could establish a custom (or even if a general one was established) scale for what our ratings mean the AI could compare it to that instead, which would be helpful.

posts.title: Mood/pace update automation
posts.description: Disclaimer: I know it's not the first time it's been mentioned and the possibility of this purely depends on tech stack/cost. So many books on TSG have significantly wrong pace/moods that were set when the book only had a few reviews and over time more accurate data was collected. Currently every change requires a separate ticket to Abbie which seems very inefficient and time consuming both for her and for people who are bothered by incorrect tags. Would it be too costly to have an automated background job that runs every time the review with mood/pace is added to a book, so that the tag data is always accurate?

posts.title: Pause/Unpause button
posts.description: So first of all I love the pause/unpause feature. However, I would love an easier way to pause and unpause. Currently, you have to click view all > click the drop down menu > the select pause/resume. I’d love to just have a button ( maybe with the universal pause/unpause icons) in addition to having it on the drop down. I’m usually pausing or resuming multiple books at a time so it would be nice to have a way to more quickly do this. Additionally, I sometimes accidentally select the wrong status and then I have to go into the journal entries to fix it. A button would make that less likely to happen.

posts.title: See Star Rating as a Grouping
posts.description: I'd love to be able to select multiple star-ratings (like 4 stars and higher) rather than having to go in and view each separately (i.e viewing 4, 4.25, 4.5, and 5). For me, 4 stars and higher, I'd recommend to others so I'd like to be able to see all of those options at once. And it'd be nice to be able to sort these (highest to lowest rating or date read maybe) :)

posts.title: Sharable graphics for tags
posts.description: I really love the monthly and early pictures of stats and book covers you get. and I would love to have that option also for book tags. then I could use those cover pictures as a sort of visualization of books i want to read, or books of a specific topic, or whatever i am tagging.

posts.title: Moods/Paces should change based on reviews
posts.description: I've seen a lot of books where the moods or pace don't fit at all and don't reflect the reviews at all either. I don't know how moods or paces are selected but I feel they should reflect the reviews and also change based on them.

posts.title: Keep moods and genres the same for editions
posts.description: There are some books where the "main" edition has more genres and moods added but smaller editions don't have them. I wish those categories would stay the same for all editions.

posts.title: Recommended Books for Friends
posts.description: I've been really leaning in to giving books as gifts for the past few years, and while I usually don't have a problem thinking of a book that I love that I think a friend would like, sometimes they have pretty different taste than me. I feel like it would be super cool to basically be able to get a peek into what their "Up Next Suggestions" would be to get the ideas flowing, with maybe a few additions: - Is there a book that I read recently that is on their TBR? - Is there a book that is on both of our TBRs so we could read them together? - Is there a book in the mood/genre that they have been reading the most in the past few months that maybe isn't on their TBR? I love to surprise people with things they haven't heard of yet. I feel like this could really enhance bookish gift giving, not just at this time of year, but for birthdays too :)

posts.title: Sort challenges by newest created when browsing challenges
Pages read in past month on Streaks page
posts.description: I would love to see a data point on the streaks page to see how much I've read in the past month, a Total number and an average. I read a minimum of a page per day, so I would love to see a real value for how much I read on average and total, compared to the previous period! I feel like this would look great in the new design style, like the reading challenges and reviews section!

posts.title: Genre: Children's Picture Books
posts.description: There is middle grade, childrens, ya, and adult. However, picture books are a very specific type of children's book. Someone looking for a picture book will NOT want anything else. It would be really useful to me to have this filter as a librarian and school teacher. I currently have almost 400 saved in a tag as jpic (Juvinile Picture Books). I know there should be more but I haven't gone though all my "childrens" books yet (a little over 300) to see which of those I should also tag as picture books.

posts.title: Audiobook filter in recommendations
posts.description: It would be really lovely as a primarily audiobook listener to have a filler in the recommendations for books that have an audiobook version. There have been quite a few times I have found a perfect fit through the recommendations, but couldn’t enjoy it because i didn’t know there wasn’t an audiobook version and I’m very dyslexic.

posts.title: Include created, completed Reading Challenges in Community news Feed
posts.description: I would love to see the community newsfeed include reading challenges that a user your completed, (including myself). Also reading challenges that a user created.

posts.title: Offer charts based on number of pages read or minutes listened instead of number of books read
posts.description: I have set year-long goals for pages read and minutes listened. But when I view the Stats tab, all of the charts appear to be using number of books read as the basis of the data. As a result, I do not have a real apples-to-apples comparison of my goals and stats. I thought I could change this as a Plus user by creating custom charts. Even though I can select pages as a measurement, I do not think I can splice it with other dimensions (e.g. book type, mood, genre, etc.). It would be cool to be able to toggle between different sources of data for the charts. Here is an example of how the charts may give a different outlook based on number of pages read: Book 1 - Nonfiction, 650 pages Book 2 - Fiction, 300 pages Book 3 - Fiction, 150 pages Chart based on books would show that 67% of my reading is Fiction. Chart based on pages would show that 41% of my reading is fiction.

posts.title: DNF books in Reading Challenges
posts.description: I made a "Read or Release" reading challenge this year to either read or let go of books I have owned more than five years. I can add books that I DNF to the challenge, but they don't show towards the number of the challenge. Don't know how many people would want this, but sometimes not reading a book and giving it away is an accomplishment! And I'd like to be able to count that toward the challenge.

posts.title: Select from entire list of content warnings
posts.description: The current system of adding content warnings works well when you know exactly what you’re going to type for each severity rating. But I think it would be helpful to also have the option to open the entire list, and then click-through to be able to choose minor, moderate, or explicit. Right now the primary input focus is on minor/moderate/explicit and I’d like the option for the primary input to be the actual content warning and then severity second.

posts.title: New to me author filter on TBR
posts.description: Under the TBR statistics i really think there should be some type of category or something pointing out new authors that's on your TBR. This could help witth reader's fatigue or if you just want to read something by a completely new author.

posts.title: Logging rereads is confusing for new users
posts.description: Just wanted to pass along some feedback from a friend who is a newer user of the app! She couldn't figure out how to log a re-read other than setting beginning and ending dates after she was already finished, which meant that she was losing her streak since she couldn't track her progress. My own experience with this is that I feel a little nervous any time I change the status of an edition I've already read, whether it's because a book has sat in "Currently Reading" for too long and I actually need to start over from the beginning, or because I've previously finished a book and want to read it again. I'm not sure why it feels like it will be a destructive action to change the status, even though I've done it multiple times, but it does! I'm overprotective of my journal entries haha, especially now that I've been using them to actually log quotes etc.

posts.title: Likes and dislikes to reviews
posts.description: An option to like and dislike reviews, accompanied with the possibility to order reviews based on the number of like, or like to dislike ratio. It's my understanding that you guys are trying to stay away from any feature that would turn the app into a type of social network, but liles/dislikes to reviews could push more thought out, thorough revies to the top, so users who are undecided on where or not they should read a book could find them more easily.

posts.title: block authors/books from suggestions page
posts.description: I want to block (after seeing that Fable can do this) problematic and harmful authors' books from my suggestions page. I can't find anything on desktop or Android that allows me to say I'm not interested, at the very least, to get out of my suggestion pool.

posts.title: Timeline / gantt chart for books read
posts.description: I tend to read a lot of books at one time and would love to see a timeline of my reading almost like a Gantt chart. I loved seeing the average time spent on a book but want to see my reading habits visually represented over a year

posts.title: Option to include a DNF books in reading goal
posts.description: I like to count certain books as part of my reading goal if I dnfed past a certain point. Maybe a prompt that asks you if you would like to count it still.

posts.title: New reading challenge type - read certain number of books from a list of specific books
posts.description: Hi, I would like to see a type of a reading challenge where I can create a list of books to choose from and the goal is to pick and finish only a certain number of them, where reader can choose which ones. Would be nice for school assignments and some curated thematic challenges where reading everything isn't the goal.

posts.title: TBR Reminders in Regular Search Results
posts.description: I have a ton of books on my TBR and I would love to be able to see forgotten matches at the top of the list when I'm using the main search bar. For example -- searching "garden" would bring up the generic search results that mention the word garden, but would simultaneously search your to-read list for "garden" in the background. If there were any hits in the TBR search, a message/button would pop up above the generic results offering to bring you to those results. (maybe something like "6 books you've marked as to-read might be a good fit")

posts.title: Stats for money spend on books
posts.description: It would be nice to be able to track the money spend on books when buying them (marking them as owned) and get stats for that. Edit: I currently use Google Sheets to track the monthly spending on books during the year but since I love StoryGraph so much and would like to keep all my bookish things related information in one place this would be a great feature for me.

posts.title: Adding a "deadline" to Up Next books
posts.description: Hello! If it's possible to add a 'deadline' date or 'to be read by' date for Up Next books, that would be amazing and would help me use Storygraph more often! Thanks!

posts.title: Paranormal Genre
posts.description: Could we add the paranormal Genre under TBR search?

posts.title: Visualizations for Mood, Pace, etc
posts.description: I would love if we could come up with a way to visualize the Mood, Pace, Character vs Plot, and all the others. I think the sections with only three options would be easy enough to manage with stacked bar charts, but not sure how to show the Moods section since there are so many options.

posts.title: Add Filter by "No cover or missing cover"
posts.description: Would be nice to be able to filter my TBR or read to find all the titles I added that at the time did not have a cover out so that they could be added/updated. Could be nice to be able to just filter by any missing info such as cover, blurb, pub date etc.

posts.title: Give TBR books a "priority"
posts.description: I love the "up next" feature, but as a chronic mood reader who is usually reading 10+ books, I find that I'm always going off the rails. It would be cool to be able to mark books as high, medium, or low priority. Then it could be a sorting criteria when looking for a new book to read in my massive TBR. That way I could differentiate between books that I'm extremely interested in reading vs stuff I'd like to read if I get around to it.

posts.title: Manually set end of day time
posts.description: I often read late at night/into the early morning. When I log the reading, it adds the journal entry for the day I'm logging - but when I've read into the early morning I count that as a continuation of the day before. I'd like to be able to set the "end of day" to a time of my choosing (say, 4am) - meaning that any reading entries added between midnight and that set time are automatically attributed to the previous day rather than the day of the logging. (For example, if I start reading at 11:30pm on 1st November and finish/log reading at 1am 2nd November, currently that logs as a reading session on 2nd November. I'd like instead for the journal to use the 1st November date.) I know I can manually change the date, but it's a bit of a faff having to do that every time and having it done automatically would be great!

posts.title: Ability to add another exclusive shelf
posts.description: I’d really like the ability to add extra exclusive shelves, in addition to currently reading, read, and TBR. I use this on Goodreads to denote books that I own, but haven’t and probably won’t read. I don’t want them clogging up my TBR but I don’t want to lose track of them completely. To me, this is an important feature that GR has and SG doesn’t.

posts.title: Filter to Exclude Books Marked “Read”
posts.description: Currently the filter allows us to exclude books from our TBR or marked as owned when viewing recommendations and popular now, but we need a filter to exclude books we have already read.

posts.title: reading and listening a book at the same time
posts.description: Sometimes I switch between listening and reading a book with the audible narration feature. I would love to track this correctly as pages read or minutes listened respectively, as I would like my stats to represent the reality as close a possible. Right now I try to choose whether I log it as pages or minutes based on what I think I will do the majority of the book, but it doesn't feel quite right.

posts.title: Add most often read section to profile page
posts.description: Similar to how 5-star reads are displayed, I'd like to see a list of my most frequently re-read books. For me at least, my re-reads are often guilty pleasures that don't have the highest rating so it would be fun to surface those somehow.

posts.title: Easily share books to Instagram Stories
posts.description: It would be cool to share books that I read with my star rating to my Instagram stories.

posts.title: Filter recs by whether friends read them
posts.description: When looking at book recommendations, it would be great to filter results to only show books reviewed by TSG friends so I can see where we overlap (and save me clicking through)

posts.title: Bookmark Reading Challenges
posts.description: I often come across reading challenges that I don't want to join (for example because I usually don't do yearly reading challenges, or because I don't want to read books for all the prompts) but that I find interesting because they have nice prompts and I'd like to go back to the challenge and use it to find new books for my tbr down the line. In that case, I'd love to be able to bookmark a challenge, instead of joining it, so I can access my bookmarks directly in the app and don't have to keep them in my browser (as I do now).

posts.title: Recommendations feature for challenges
posts.description: I wish there was a way to recommend books for specific prompts without it being added to my challenge.

posts.title: Discussion of Book Challenges
posts.description: It would be nice have a discussion forum for the book challenges or even individual books.

posts.title: Clickable "Number of books and pages" graph
posts.description: I would love to be able to click on any books or pages dot in the "Number of books and pages" graph and be able to see the books it encompasses. My current graph shows me at 3 books and 1,600ish pages in March and I would love to see how it thinks I've read that many pages.

posts.title: Top Readers Stat
posts.description: I'd love a stat on each book page that shows which users have read this book the most! I have a friend who's read one (not old/wildly popular) book 24 times, and I would be so curious to know if they're the top reader of that book. Apps like Spotistats have things like that for songs, and they're called "top listeners," and it's super interesting to look at and see my friends on it.

posts.title: Sort Giveaways by date added
posts.description: I'd like a way to tell which giveaways I've looked at and if there are any new ones since the last time I browsed.

posts.title: Applying filters to any search results
posts.description: I would like to be able to search for an author and filter the results by language and/or format. As of now, these filters can only be used to filter editions of a single book. It would also be nice to be able to view all / selected books in a given language or books available in e-book or audiobook, without knowing an author.

posts.title: Download Stats
posts.description: I would love to be able to download my states as an excel sheet straight from story graphy

posts.title: Page count input field as a filter option
posts.description: This time of year, I'm always helping friends with recs for novellas, novelettes etc. so that they can wrap up various book bingos and reading challenges. This happens at other points of the year too, but it's a staple of every December! Filtering my Read list by low-to-high page count is an unreliable mess—a lot of audio-only families and other messy/incomplete book families show up first and the sorting is beyond untrustworthy. I would really like to be able to be able to filter my Read list for books under, e.g., 150 pages.

posts.title: See who finished a reading challenge
posts.description: It would be interesting to see who already finished a reading challenge (maybe with dates when joined, when finished and how long it took for each promt?)

posts.title: Recommendations should have to read and read filtered out by default
Reading Challenge Stats
posts.description: Not much to explain here. Would be so fun to see comparisons between books within a reading challenge - such as ratings.

posts.title: Filter By # Times Re-Read
posts.description: I know that when you click into the journal for an individual book you can see all the dates for each time you have read a book, but I would love to be able to pull a list of all books that I have read multiple times! (All books I've read 2 times, 3 times, 4 times, etc.)

posts.title: Don't show 'Enter Giveaway' button if a book is marked as Owned
Turn off 'giveaways' menu
posts.description: The top menubar is starting to feel a little cluttered, esp with the new 'giveaways' addition. I really liked the minimal style of The StoryGraph and I'm wondering whether we could (maybe as a plus thing, or just for everyone) have an option in settings to never see the "Giveaways". I know some people will love that and want it in their menu, perhaps, but I am pretty sure I'll never use / want to use the Giveaways, so I'm fine keeping the less busy menu.

posts.title: Ability to Read Portions of Books Without Starting from Page 1
posts.description: I do a LOT of reading in graduate school, and often my professors will assign specific portions or chapters from a book without assigning the entire book. It would be awesome if I could log pages read without having to start from page 1 of a book. For example, I might have 300 pages of reading over the course of a semester that come from 15 different books, and none of that counts towards my reading goals since I'm not able to record sections of pages read. If I need to read page 247-280 for class, I can't add it to my StoryGraph tracking because I'm not reading pages 1-247 as well! (Hopefully this makes sense!)

posts.title: Add "Editor" role
posts.description: Please consider adding the Editor role to book pages. It's particularly important for anthologies, where the editor's name is written on the cover. Lee Child is not the author of this book: https://app.thestorygraph.com/books/7b82c2e5-4c16-48f5-8a2c-f3e787e60c54 . He is its editor. The book includes stories by several authors that need to be added, but Lee Child is not one of them. I hope my point is clear.

posts.title: Different "reading preferences" profiles
posts.description: Hi.
